newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 11.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Tuesday's Daily Variety:

* WASHINGTON - President Clinton is expected Tuesday to increase pressure on broadcasters to provide free airtime to political campaigns by repeating his endorsement of pending campaign reform legislation. Clinton has already endorsed legislation asking broadcasters to set aside time for political campaign commercials. Tuesday he will speak at a D.C. conference entitled "Free Air Time and Campaign Reform."

* NEW YORK - Nicolas Cage and Will Smith are sealing deals to star together in "Snake Eyes" by Viacom's Paramount Pictures for director Brian De Palma, sources said. The project, which is being produced by De Palma and by its screenwriter, David Koepp, is scheduled to go before the cameras August 1. It involves a detective who witnesses the assassination of the U.S. secretary of defense during a heavyweight boxing title match.

* SYDNEY - "Dante's Peak" had a very good but not incandescent foreign debut in Japan, while in Europe, audiences showed plenty of money for "Jerry Maguire." "101 Dalmatians" scampered into four European territories with impressive figures, "Mars Attacks!" pulled in $9.2 million overseas from holdovers and several debuts, and "The English Patient" wowed Australia and Spain .

* NEW YORK - PolyGram and Interscope have given the green light for a movie romance with Robin Williams, "What Dreams May Come." The project, budgeted between $65-$70 million, is the most ambitious project the companies have done together.

* NEW YORK - Oscar nominee Frances McDormand is in serious talks to star in "The Trade," a drama written by Cara Lindstrom and directed by Angela Pope for Sydney Pollack's Mirage Enterprises. The producers are also negotiating for Nicole Kidman to join McDormand in the other female lead role.

* NEW YORK - John Goldwyn has been promoted to the newly created position of president of Paramount Motion Pictures. The move paves the way for Executive Vice President of Production Michelle Manning to step in to the president of production post that Goldwyn previously held, although that issue is unresolved.
